Glossary of geography terms (A–M).fact: magma Molten rock containing liquids, crystals, and dissolved gases that forms within the upper part of the Earth's mantle and crust. When erupted onto the Earth's surface, it is called lava.

Glossary of geography terms (A–M).subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of geography terms (A–M).question: The angle made with the horizontal by the _____'s magnetic field lines
Glossary of geography terms (A–M).fact: Because compass needles always point to magnetic north, and because the Magnetic North Pole and the Geographic North Pole are not in precisely the same location, the north direction indicated by a compass may be slightly different from the direction of geographic north, depending on the user's location on the Earth. Glossary of geography terms (A–M).fact: magnetic pole Either of the two poles of the Earth's true magnetic field – the Magnetic North Pole or the Magnetic South Pole.

Glossary of geography terms (A–M).subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of geography terms (A–M).question: mammilated _____ and rounded in appearance, used of various landforms of different sizes from individual rocks to entire landscapes
Glossary of geography terms (A–M).fact: mammilated Smooth and rounded in appearance, used of various landforms of different sizes from individual rocks to entire landscapes.

Glossary of geography terms (A–M).question: The mantle is about _____ (1,800 mi) thick, making up 84% of the Earth's volume and 67% of its mass
Glossary of geography terms (A–M).fact: The mantle is about 2,900 kilometers (1,800 mi) thick, making up 84% of the Earth's volume and 67% of its mass.

Glossary of geography terms (A–M).subject: Health & Medicine

Glossary of geography terms (A–M).fact: In medieval Europe, a march was the land surrounding a border between realms, or a neutral buffer zone under the joint control of two or more realms with conflicting laws or territorial claims.

Glossary of geography terms (A–M).subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of geography terms (A–M).question: Any section of the _____'s crust which is demarcated by faults or flexures and tends to retain its internal structure while being displaced as a whole
Glossary of geography terms (A–M).fact: Any section of the Earth's crust which is demarcated by faults or flexures and tends to retain its internal structure while being displaced as a whole. mean sea level (MSL) The average sea level of one or more of the Earth's coastal bodies of water, such as oceans and seas, or at a particular location, from which heights such as elevation and altitude are measured.

Glossary of geography terms (A–M).subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of geography terms (A–M).question: Mediterranean climate Any climate characterized by mild, rainy winters and hot, dry summers, as experienced in the _____
Glossary of geography terms (A–M).fact: Mediterranean climate Any climate characterized by mild, rainy winters and hot, dry summers, as experienced in the Mediterranean Basin.

Glossary of geography terms (A–M).fact: meridional Of, relating to, or characteristic of the south, especially of the inhabitants of a southern region or territory, in particular southern Europe.

Glossary of geography terms (A–M).question: Mohorovičić discontinuity _____ discontinuity, Moho boundary, or simply Moho
Glossary of geography terms (A–M).fact: Mohorovičić discontinuity Also Moho discontinuity, Moho boundary, or simply Moho.

Glossary of geography terms (A–M).question: muskeg _____ name for a bog, used primarily in Alaska and western Canada
Glossary of geography terms (A–M).fact: muskeg Another name for a bog, used primarily in Alaska and western Canada.

Glossary of geography terms (A–M).question: chain A unit of length equal to 66 feet (20.117 m), used especially in public land surveys in the _____; 10 square chains is equal to 1 acre (0.40 hectares)

Glossary of geography terms (A–M).subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of geography terms (A–M).question: The mantle is about 2,900 kilometers (1,800 mi) thick, making up 84% of the _____'s volume and 67% of its mass

Glossary of geography terms (N–Z).subject: Health & Medicine
Glossary of geography terms (N–Z).question: nautical mile A unit of distance traditionally defined as the length equal to one minute of arc (1⁄60 of one degree) along a meridian of the _____
Glossary of geography terms (N–Z).fact: nautical mile A unit of distance traditionally defined as the length equal to one minute of arc (1⁄60 of one degree) along a meridian of the Earth. Because the Earth is not a perfect sphere, the length of one minute of arc at the Equator differs from that measured at the geographic poles; thus the modern internationally agreed-upon standard defines the nautical mile as the average of these two extremes: 1,852 metres (6,076 feet; 1.151 miles).
